title: Create Table [FOREIGN KEY Practice]
description:
## Foreign Keys in Action
Let's see what happens when foreign keys protect your data.

With foreign keys ON:
- Insert a ticket for server that EXISTS -> works
- Insert a ticket for server that DOESN'T EXIST -> rejected

The tickets table and servers table from last lesson are already set up.


---
## Assignment:
Insert two tickets:
1. Title `'Disk full'` for server_id `1` (exists)
2. Title `'Memory leak'` for server_id `2` (exists)

Then try to understand: what would happen if you used server_id `999`?
setupCode: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; CREATE TABLE servers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); INSERT INTO servers VALUES (1, 'prod-1'), (2, 'prod-2'); CREATE TABLE tickets (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, server_id INTEGER, priority TEXT DEFAULT 'low', FOREIGN KEY (server_id) REFERENCES servers(id));
runHarness: SELECT tickets.title, servers.name FROM tickets INNER JOIN servers ON tickets.server_id = servers.id;
expectedOutput:
title | name
Disk full | prod-1
Memory leak | prod-2
